title: Blind by Design: Computational Supplement
description: Computational supplement to 'Blind by Design: Quantum Error Correction, Functional Incompatibility and the Value of Evidence' (Lex et Ratio Working Paper LXR-2026-PHI-BBDQEC-WP) and to its technical companion, 'Sign-Blind Recovery, Record Leakage and Model Misspecification in Quantum Error Correction: Worked Numerical Cases'. Seven scripts: a numerical check of Proposition 5.2, which bounds what the classical record of an approximately function-preserving inquiry can reveal about an encoded quantum state (leak at most 2√ε for functional defect ε in diamond norm), on a toric-code and a repetition-code instrument, with a comparison of the complementary output and the classical record, and of pointwise and uniform repair over all channels, with and without the syndrome history; a three-qubit repetition-code instrument showing observation-relative and function-relative blindness; an independent numerical check of a toric-code sign-symmetry result (Özgüler 2026, Proposition 1); a construction audit of Stim/PyMatching surface-code simulations; and a continuous error-correction simulation in which a misspecified detector efficiency is detected and repaired from the records already held; and a two-round extension of the comparison between repairs that know the sign of a coherent rotation and repairs that must serve both signs, with the two-round syndrome history discarded or used; and an analysis of that comparison by entanglement infidelity, over up to 300 rounds against an idealised twirl, and under calibration error. Includes the complete output of each reference run and the reliance note on the preprint result used in the paper.
